# Eval scorecard

<!-- Generated by scripts/build_eval_scorecard.py. Do not edit by hand; run the script. -->

Scores per specialist and dataset, as committed in `agents/python/evals/baselines/python-inproc-replay/` (baselines are keyed by setup: stack, target and model).

**Read this first.** These numbers are a regression signal, not a quality measurement. Every case was answered from a replay fixture recorded on `gpt-4.1-2025-04-14` (107 fixtures) between 2026-08-21 and 2026-11-24, and the scorer is deterministic: groundedness is a database check, correctness is a tool or route match, and completeness is a keyword check, not a judge model. A score tells you the recorded answers still pass the current code and prompts, which is what the PR job named Replay regression checks. It says nothing about how a different model, or the same model today, would do. Each dataset has five or six cases, so one flipped case moves a score by 0.1 or more, and the score is a property of the recording session as much as of the system (see `agents/python/evals/fixtures/README.md`).

## Live reference baselines (not a quality guarantee)

**These are live runs, not replay.** Each row is one sitting of one model with an LLM judge, taken through the in-process target on a freshly seeded database. With one repeat there is no spread: a single flipped case moves a suite by a few points, and a rerun can move it too. They are stored under their own setup key and the replay gate never compares against them. A self-judged run says so in the Judge column. A case the judge could not score (content filter) is noted beside Passed, with how many of those the less strict keyword fallback scored instead. Cost is the tokens times the price in `config/pricing/models.yaml` with cached input billed at the full rate, so it is an upper bound, and it excludes the judge calls.

## Community-submitted, not verified by the maintainers

Results people ran on their own provider and model and contributed under `agents/python/evals/community/` (format and rules: `agents/python/evals/community/README.md`). Each file passed `python -m evals.community_validate` when it was merged and the test suite re-checks it, which shows it is well formed and, where records are attached, that the scores follow from them. It does not show that the run happened, and the maintainers did not re-run it. Setups differ (provider, model, judge, repeats), so rows here are not comparable with each other or with the reference baselines above. Overall is shown for quality suites and pass rate for safety suites, as mean +/- standard deviation across repeats when there were two or more.

No community results have been submitted yet.

## Regenerating

```bash
uv run --project agents/python python -m scripts.build_eval_scorecard
```

Run it after a baseline changes (`--update-baseline`, see `agents/python/evals/README.md`). CI runs the same command with `--check` and fails when this page no longer matches the baselines.
